paths.description: Homepage and news portal landing template, including consent, navigation, feeds, responsive states and primary discovery journey.
Politics section listing, representative of editorial category/listing templates.
Current politics article, representative of the core reading and shareable news-detail journey.
Site search results for “economia”, representing the content-finding form flow.
Live/video hub, representing the media-heavy viewing template.
Non-existent URL used to inspect HTTP/error recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to a dark system preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot is visually the same light page and modal as the default capture; CSS probing found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface, text, border and media colors using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found six running animations, including two roughly 80-second animations, and no prefers-reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable auto-advancing and non-essential motion under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce while preserving necessary state feedback.

findings.summary: Route changes do not expose a coherent transition treatment.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition-name or ::view-transition rules across the MPA navigation surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Use progressive cross-document View Transitions for section/article navigation, with reduced-motion handling and a no-transition fallback.

findings.summary: Long news pages provide no position-aware reading chrome.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 32,812 px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query or progress treatment; the header remains generic site chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight reading/progress affordance or scroll-state-aware compact header on long listing and article templates.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures every representative page on first load.
findings.evidence: Homepage, article, section, live, mobile and 404 screenshots all show a large modal covering the primary content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Avoid blocking editorial content before a choice. Offer compact, dismissible consent controls and defer non-essential vendors until an explicit choice.

findings.summary: The modal consent experience is built from custom div dialogs rather than a native modal primitive.
findings.evidence: The UI probe found four div[role=dialog] nodes, zero dialog elements, zero popovers and no aria-modal on the visible consent dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> for the modal flow with correct focus trapping, inert background, Escape/cancel behavior and an explicit non-consent path.

findings.summary: Consent and market/sports chrome crowd out the editorial content.
findings.evidence: On mobile the consent panel consumes almost the full 360×800 viewport; on desktop the first view is dominated by consent and multiple chrome bands rather than a lead story.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce first-view chrome, keep the consent choice compact, and prioritize the lead editorial content.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no @container rules despite reusable cards, rails and carousels appearing in different-width regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable card, rail and navigation components while retaining viewport fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is frequently invisible and several controls are too small.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found many focused links with outline-style none and no box shadow; visible controls measured 24×24, 32×32 and 36×36 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and enlarge touch targets to at least 44×44 CSS px or equivalent spacing.

findings.summary: Loading and responsiveness miss the good Core Web Vitals experience.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 3.5 s and TBT 550 ms; the independent trace observed LCP 7.55 s and 384 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the lead content/LCP image, defer non-critical scripts and ads, and split long tasks.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 4.6 s main-thread work and 1.9 s script bootup; the trace contains a 360 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or delay non-essential third-party execution, code-split page features and yield long work with scheduler/task chunking.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive request and byte payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 213 requests and 6.56 MB, including 122 images/3.98 MB and 41 scripts/1.83 MB; two font stylesheets are high-priority parser-inserted blockers.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a route budget, reduce initial image count, preload only the actual LCP resource, self-host/subset fonts and defer below-fold dependencies.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused code ship on the landing page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 722 KiB unused JavaScript and 97 KiB unused CSS; ad, identity and social bundles are major contributors.
findings.suggestedFix: Load advertising, identity, social and feature bundles only when the related surface is used; purge unused CSS per template.

findings.summary: Important controls and media affordances have broken accessible names or ARIA.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unnamed buttons/links, prohibited ARIA, 8 SVG images without text alternatives and 12 label/name mismatches.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a stable accessible name that includes its visible label, remove prohibited ARIA and label decorative versus meaningful SVG correctly.

findings.summary: Multiple text treatments fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found 26 contrast failures, including green financial values at 2.27:1 and pale sports labels as low as 1.58:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace pale semantic colors with tokens that meet WCAG AA in every state and verify with automated and visual contrast tests.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and the accessibility tree are not reliable.
findings.evidence: Focused links commonly computed to outline none; Lighthouse also reports an ill-formed agent/accessibility tree and invalid tabpanel/ARIA usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Define consistent :focus-visible styles and repair tab/tabpanel ownership, permitted ARIA attributes and focus order.

findings.summary: Small targets and unlabeled live-media frames reduce inclusive access.
findings.evidence: The target probe found 24–36 px controls, while the live page probe found several iframes with empty titles and no exposed caption tracks.
findings.suggestedFix: Enlarge controls, title embedded frames and ensure live and recorded media expose captions/transcripts.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a React hydration error and a 404 request to the favorites API.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the server/client markup mismatch and avoid firing favorites requests for missing or anonymous resources.

findings.summary: Image markup and delivery are inconsistent and wasteful.
findings.evidence: The image probe found 3 images without dimensions, 60 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 73 without srcset, 91 legacy-format assets and 55 empty/missing alt values requiring editorial review.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, prefer AVIF/WebP and provide intentional alt text.

findings.summary: The page requests notification permission on load and misses BFCache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed notification-on-start and reported that an in-flight iframe navigation prevented BFCache restoration.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notifications only after a clear user action and stop/cancel subframe work so completed navigations can enter BFCache.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint is broken and returns an index-confusing error document.
findings.evidence: /sitemap.xml returns HTTP 404 with an application error body that contains both noindex and index robots tags plus a homepage canonical.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid sitemap index with HTTP 200, list it in robots.txt, and ensure error documents have a single noindex policy and self-consistent canonical behavior.

findings.summary: Baseline response defenses and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and nosniff are present, but CSP and HSTS are absent; 11 cookies were reported without Secure and all 11 use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS and Secure cookies; use Lax/Strict unless cross-site behavior is necessary.

findings.summary: The default load has a very large third-party tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 32 third-party origins and 5 known trackers; the HAR attributes 183 requests and 5.46 MB to non-main origins before a consent choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors until consent, consolidate analytics, shorten identifier lifetimes and enforce a measured third-party budget.

findings.summary: Notification permission is initiated without user context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse traced a notification-on-start request to notifpush.com/scripts/wpn2.js.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove permission requests from startup and ask only after a user enables a clearly explained alert feature.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer and permissions defenses are not declared.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (and X-Frame-Options for legacy coverage), strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The consent wall lacks a direct reject choice while offering immediate consent.
findings.evidence: The visible dialog exposes only Consent and Manage options; the probe found no reject button, while the copy names 420 partners and content remains blocked.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide an equally prominent Reject non-essential option beside Consent and make later reversal easy.

findings.summary: The newsletter form does not expose robust required/error semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found the EMAIL and terms checkbox are not required and have no aria-describedby error association; the consent checkbox starts aria-invalid=false.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints where semantically required, validate after interaction and connect concise errors with aria-describedby/live announcements.

findings.summary: The page ships too many unoptimized image variants for an editorial landing page.
findings.evidence: Image evidence found 91 legacy-format images, 73 without srcset and 60 below-fold images loaded eagerly; HAR image transfer reached 3.98 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP variants, lazy-load below-fold media and make editorial image budgets part of publishing.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The load performs 213 requests across 33 origins with 4.6 s main-thread work; much of the unused script is advertising, identity and analytics code.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential work on consent/visibility, batch analytics and remove redundant vendors and idle background tasks.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts and media dominate the resource budget.
findings.evidence: HAR records 183 third-party requests and 5.46 MB, while Lighthouse reports a 4.25 MiB page under its run and 722 KiB potentially unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce per-template third-party, image, font and script budgets; defer video and ad dependencies until intent.

findings.summary: The settled homepage has a large memory and DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: Heap baseline contains 1,031,746 heap nodes and 60.0 MB self size; the live DOM probe counted 12,846 elements for one landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize or paginate deep feeds, avoid rendering hidden consent/vendor trees up front and release below-fold component state.

taskList.title: Replace the blocking, reject-less consent wall and prevent pre-consent vendor loading
Cut initial script, image and third-party cost to restore fast loading
Fix accessible names, ARIA, focus, target size and contrast
Deploy CSP/HSTS, defensive policies and secure cookie defaults
Stop notification permission requests on startup
Repair image markup and responsive delivery
Restore a valid sitemap and consistent indexing signals
Respect dark mode and reduced motion
Resolve hydration/API console errors and BFCache blockers
Improve component-level responsiveness and navigation continuity
